name: Ticket to Ride
edition: Base game (North America map), 2015 reprint rules

setup.text: Put the board in the middle of the table.
Shuffle the Train Car cards and deal 4 to each player.
Put the rest of the Train Car deck beside the board and turn 5 cards face up.
Put the Longest Path bonus card face up beside the board.
Shuffle the Destination Tickets and deal 3 to each player. Everyone keeps at least 2; returned tickets go under the ticket deck. Tickets stay secret until final scoring.
Take 45 trains in one colour and the matching scoring marker. Put the marker on Start.
The most experienced traveller goes first; play runs clockwise.

turn.summary: Do exactly one of three things.
steps: Draw 2 Train Car cards, each from the face-up row or blind from the deck. Replace a face-up card as soon as you take it.
Claim one route: discard a set of matching cards equal to its length, place your trains on it and score it straight away. Grey routes take a set of any one colour.
Draw 3 Destination Tickets and keep at least 1; the rest go under the deck.

end: When a player has 0, 1 or 2 trains left at the end of their turn, every player, including that one, takes one last turn.

scoring.text: Routes are scored as they are claimed: length 1 = 1, 2 = 2, 3 = 4, 4 = 7, 5 = 10, 6 = 15 points.
Reveal tickets: add the value of each completed ticket and subtract the value of each one not completed.
Longest continuous path scores 10 points. If players tie for it, each of them scores the 10.

tiebreak: Most completed Destination Tickets, then whoever holds the Longest Path card.

missed.text: Only one route of each double route can be used; once one side is claimed the other is closed.
One player can never claim both routes of a double route.
Locomotives are wild. Taking a face-up locomotive is your whole draw, and you cannot take a face-up locomotive as your second card. A locomotive drawn blind still lets you draw two.
If three of the five face-up cards are locomotives, discard all five and turn up five new ones.
There is no hand limit, and you can claim only one route per turn.
A new route does not have to connect to your earlier routes.
When the deck runs out, shuffle the discards into a new deck.
